subject: Impact of Overturning Roe v. Wade
overview: Medford Bytes hosts Danielle Balocca and Chelli Keshavan interviewed state representative candidate Nicole Mossalam about the Supreme Court's decision overturning Roe v. Wade. Mossalam discussed the ruling's implications for reproductive healthcare, broader privacy rights, and the need for legislative action in Massachusetts.

items.title: Introduction and Casual Opening
items.summary: Co-hosts Danielle Balocca and Chelli Keshavan introduced state representative candidate Nicole Mossalam, who briefly discussed local restaurants in the area.

items.title: Personal and Professional Impact of Roe v. Wade Reversal
items.summary: Mossalam described how the overturning of Roe v. Wade strengthened her campaign motivation and shared personal experiences regarding reproductive healthcare, right-to-privacy precedents, and LGBTQ+ parental rights.

items.title: State Legislative Role and Massachusetts Protections
items.summary: Mossalam warned that reproductive rights in Massachusetts are not fully secure, noting the close veto-override margin of the 2020 ROE Act and the need for proactive state and federal coalition-building.

items.title: Comprehensive Healthcare and Systemic Support for Families
items.summary: Mossalam argued for broadening pro-life policies to include practical family support like diaper coverage and workplace protections, citing her personal healthcare challenges during pregnancy.

items.title: Sexual Assault and Bodily Autonomy
items.summary: The discussion addressed the underreporting of sexual violence and how abortion restrictions intersect with trauma and the denial of bodily autonomy.

items.title: Interstate Coalitions, Surveillance, and Constitutional Reform
items.summary: Mossalam emphasized building interstate coalitions, guarding against digital surveillance, regulating crisis pregnancy centers, and pursuing federal constitutional amendments to protect fundamental rights.
